title: Magnetic monster NGC 1275
caption: The galaxy NGC 1275 and its gas filaments, imaged by the Hubble Space Telescope
celestial: NGC 1275 · constellation Perseus · about 250 million light-years away (source figure)
credit: NASA, ESA and Andy Fabian (University of Cambridge, UK)

recognition.text: Ranked #11 on ESA/Hubble’s published “Top 100 Images” list (an institutional selection, not an audience score).

story: Reddish, lace-like threads wrap around the bright galaxy at the center of this picture. The galaxy is NGC 1275, the giant elliptical at the heart of a galaxy cluster in the constellation Perseus, and the threads are fragile filaments of gas that Hubble's Advanced Camera for Surveys captured in fine detail.

The filaments stay cool even though the gas around them sits at roughly 55 million degrees Celsius. A magnetic field holds them together. By studying their shape, astronomers were able to estimate that field's strength for the first time, and showed how magnetism has kept the filaments from collapsing under gravity or being torn apart by the turbulent cluster over their lifetime of about 100 million years.

The filaments also reveal how energy from the galaxy's central black hole is passed on to the surrounding gas. Hubble could even separate individual threads only about 200 light-years wide, while whole filaments can stretch to 200 000 light-years.
scale: Using the source's listed field of view (3.86 x 2.99 arcminutes) and distance (250 million light years), the frame spans roughly 281,000 × 217,000 light-years. Its light set out about 250 million years before reaching the telescope.

understand.summary: Hubble's Advanced Camera for Surveys recorded this view in visible light through blue, yellow-green and red filters. The color assigned to each filter isn't published.
understand.eye: Long camera exposures gather far more light than the eye can, which is what brings out faint structures like these filaments.

behind.people: See full credit: NASA, ESA and Andy Fabian (University of Cambridge, UK)
behind.exposure: Not published on the source page.
behind.technique: Not stated by the source (single frame, stack, mosaic or panorama unknown).

explore: The entire frame spans roughly 260 000 light-years. The dark dust lanes belong to a separate spiral galaxy lying partly in front of NGC 1275, and tidal forces inside the cluster have thoroughly disrupted it. Several filaments of newborn blue stars also cross the view.
alt: A bright central galaxy surrounded by reddish, lacy filaments, with dark dust lanes and thin streaks of blue stars crossing the scene.
